Resolves #17868

Builds resolve webpack from the active project's package context and parse5 from the producer's module context. The original engine/workspace `neoPath` config selection is preserved. Markdown consumers import an engine-owned ESM asset copied from upstream marked with its license; initial/release builds produce it, npm packaging requires it, and ESM builds carry both parser assets from the supplying engine into consumer output. The thread runner uses Node with literal arguments, preserving its thread/environment options across hoisted installs and paths containing spaces.

Evidence: L2 (real filesystem, package installation, compiler subprocesses and parser execution in isolated consumer fixtures; no application UI boot claim) → L2 required (dependency-resolution and build-output ACs). No outstanding AC residual.

Change class: capability — adds the shipped marked artifact producer and its package contract while restoring installed-engine build behavior.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | CI-covered: `buildDependencyResolution.spec.mjs` executes the real runner using the unmodified package manifest emitted by `create-app`, including its runner script. It covers workspace and hoisted compilers, competing workspace/engine compiler installations, all seven threads in both environments, framework mode, and nonzero child failure. Outside-CI: the installed-package App/Data CLI matrix below. |
| AC-2 | CI-covered: the same spec invokes the actual parse5 producer from an unrelated cwd and executes its output after removing fixture dependencies. Baseline producer invocation failed on the cwd-relative entry. |
| AC-3 | [Decision and contract](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17868) recorded. CI-covered: `checkPackageContents.spec.mjs`, the actual Package Contents job, standalone parser execution, and both real source import addresses in `esmWorkspaceBuild.spec.mjs`. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: Consumer Runtime Build now compiles a fixture importing both real Markdown/content classes from an npm-installed engine. Outside-CI: four installed CLI builds and full ESM build below; no engine edits were needed for the positive runs. |

All spec paths above are under `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/`.

## Deltas from ticket

The operator's workspace challenge corrected two scope mistakes: the original `neoPath`/`webpackPath` selection is restored, and `build-all` again invokes the parser producers for workspaces. Compiler lookup is rooted in the active project's manifest so the engine's postinstall dependencies cannot override the workspace's webpack. The default generated workspace uses engine-shipped build configs; its local dev-server config and app inventory are separate surfaces.

The implementation closes the full original ticket; the earlier Node-only PR was closed without merging. Marked's upstream distribution is already self-contained, so the producer copies it and its license. The existing ESM artifact-copy stage now reads the supplying engine rather than the consumer cwd, also correcting parse5 carriage.

The consumer guard reads npm's JSON filename and packs with lifecycle scripts disabled after artifacts are prepared. Its former last-line parser consumed hook-install output as part of the filename during local validation.

The pre-existing private-runtime-cache packaging exclusion is out of scope, noted in [this defect note on #17238](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/issues/17238#issuecomment-5587677665). Package-check success here certifies its enrolled rules, not every possible private tree.

`agent-preflight`: not hosted here (the script is absent). Local pre-commit checks passed; the PR Baseline jobs will report the shared body/substrate checks.

## Test Evidence

Outside-CI installed-package receipt: packed the branch, installed that tarball into a consumer with its build tools, and imported the real `Markdown` and `app/content/Component` source modules from the fixture app. Neither `consumer/node_modules/marked` nor `neo.mjs/node_modules/marked` existed.

| Command in the consumer | Result |
|---|---|
| `node node_modules/neo.mjs/buildScripts/webpack/buildThreads.mjs -n -e dev -t data` | Compiled successfully |
| Same CLI: `-e prod -t data` | Compiled successfully |
| Same CLI: `-e dev -t app` | Compiled successfully |
| Same CLI: `-e prod -t app` | Compiled successfully |
| `node node_modules/neo.mjs/buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs` | Exit 0; full engine source emitted, both parser assets present; emitted marked parser returned the expected HTML |

The ESM build reports four optional computed-root warnings for absent workspace-addon/example/docs trees; those branches are unused by this fixture.

Negative controls:
- Restoring the dev runner and ESM copy implementation made the two focused regression arms fail (missing webpack shim, two unresolved emitted parser imports). Restoring this change returned both to green.
- In the installed copy, restoring only the two old marked import statements made the same Data build fail on both missing modules. Restoring the candidate imports returned it to green.
- The initial fixture used an incorrect app import depth and omitted two build tools; those failed runs were fixture errors and are excluded from the positive receipt.

Generated-workspace correction at `d6cdb77629`: executed the unmodified generation tasks from [create-app@d8ae9ffa](https://github.com/neomjs/create-app/tree/d8ae9ffa41acd7efe0727e11789ca769d2c4f33a), including its package/scripts, app/Viewport, config, MicroLoader and ServiceWorker. With a physical candidate engine package layout and the available toolchain, the generated `npm run build-threads -- -n -e all -t all` completed **14 compilations**, emitting all seven outputs in development and production. This exercises the generated output; the complete npx installer/network/postinstall lifecycle was not run.

The competing-compiler control fails on approved `ef75e74d2d` (engine-local poison compiler exits 91) and passes on the correction. CI retains the actual emitted manifest in `fixtures/neoAppPackage.json` and invokes its declared runner path.

*   **Expected Solution Shape:** fixing the executable resolution should not change which *workspace* the webpack **configs** are read from. A `create-app` workspace and the installed engine are different roots, and the build path has to keep distinguishing them.
*   **Patch Verdict:** Contradicts. `webpackPath` moved from `path.resolve(neoPath, 'buildScripts/webpack')` — where `neoPath` was `'./'` inside neo.mjs and `'./node_modules/neo.mjs/'` in a consumer, i.e. resolved from the **consumer's cwd** — to `path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))`, the **running script's own directory**. `parseThreads()` then reads `${webpackPath}/development/webpack.config.*`, so the config root is now pinned to the installed engine unconditionally. The generator treats these as distinct on purpose: `buildScripts/create/app.mjs:256-262` prefers a workspace-local `path.resolve(cwd, 'buildScripts/myApps.json')` and falls back to `path.resolve(__dirname, …)` only when it is absent. This change collapses that distinction for `webpackPath`.
*   **Premise Coherence:** Coheres with the ticket's premise — engine-owned addressing is right for the *executable* and for the shipped bundles, which is what I verified in round 1. It conflicts on one surface: the same reasoning applied to the **config** root removes a consumer's ability to own its build configuration.

### 🔬 Delta Depth Floor

*   **Delta challenge:** Four of the six specs in this file cannot pass on macOS, and it is **not** this PR's defect. The expectation is built from `os.tmpdir()` (`/var/folders/…`) while the subprocess reports the realpath (`/private/var/folders/…`), so the argv deep-equality fails on every macOS machine and never on Linux CI. Repo-wide sweep: **28 unit specs use `os.tmpdir()`, none uses `realpath`** — a class this PR surfaced, not introduced. It hit me directly: my first read of the arm showed "4 failed / 2 passed" on *both* sources, which looked like the poison test failing to discriminate. Naming it because the next macOS maintainer will lose the same hour.

*   **Documented search:** *"I actively checked the restored `neoPath`/`webpackPath` selection at source, the `all.mjs` guard removal against the generated workspace's own dependency list, and the poison arm as a spec/source split on both sources, and found no remaining concerns."*
